entry.title: Prospero: a new coding harness for a more civilized age
entry.summary:
I’ve been fascinated with local LLMs for a couple of years now. The better open weight models, including some that inference on regular, higher-end consumer hardware at tolerable speeds, are now reliable enough to handle simpler programming tasks. This requires a coding harness, but so far this year I’ve been disappointed by all the harness offerings. For inexplicable reasons most are built with web stacks, and consume enormous amounts of memory. At its core a coding harness is essentially curl glued to popen(). This should not require gigabytes of RAM. So I built my own: Prospero. It’s written in my C++ style with a snappy Dear ImGui docking interface. It uses around two orders of magnitude fewer resources than other harnesses without sacrificing features.

entry.title: An LC-3 Disassembler in Haskell
entry.summary: LC-3 assembly is an educational programming language. It is simple enough that complex programs can be written directly in it without needing a compiler, and thus it is often used in teaching assembly. An LC-3 textual assembly program is compiled to a binary object file by an assembler, and then executed by a virtual machine. Writing a virtual machine for LC-3 is a fun little exercise. However, in this post, we implement a disassembler for compiled LC-3 binaries back to textual assembly programs.

entry.title: tugz: a new deflate library with three applications
entry.summary:
I spent a week creating a new deflate implementation from scratch in C named tugz to provide an Info-ZIP-compatible zip program for w64devkit 2.10.1 (released today). I also replaced busybox-w32’s deflate-based unzip, gzip, gunzip, and zcat apps as well. My new deflate performs much better than zlib and on par with libdeflate. In general the new programs are substantially faster and produce slightly smaller outputs than the BusyBox equivalents, which is optimized for size than speed after all, but also compared to the original gzip and Info-ZIP you get in a typical Linux distribution. The tugz programs are CRT-free (inspect them with peports!) with first-class Windows support and better Unicode handling.

entry.title: A new, bespoke static site generator to replace Jekyll
entry.summary: My blog began as a blosxom (Perl) site running on a VPS. In 2011 I moved to the new GitHub Pages, with the site generated statically by Jekyll (Ruby) on a GitHub server. It was a no-brainer: easier, faster, and cheaper, better in every way. After 15 years of Jekyll, and spurred by a post on m4, this week I replaced it with a new, custom-built static site generator, dubbed ssg, in “C with templates” C++20. The ~8KLoC source closely follows my personal coding style including templated arenas and slices, zero dependencies, and a libc-free core. It’s wicked fast, and a complete, cold generation of my blog takes 150ms on my MacBook. That is, it’s done before Ruby would even reach Jekyll’s entry point. entry.title: My Impossible Bucket List
entry.summary:
I wrote this post for a prompt given during our local Indieweb club meeting. See more such posts. My impossible bucket list, things I would want to do/be if the realities of the world and my life did not constrain me. Here it goes: Watch the Sun die. Write a bestseller book about physics. Make them do a good remake of that one anime from the 90s I liked a lot. Finish reading all the books in my to-read list. Get rid of ALL the mosquitoes. Swim across a river. Complete this list. Cycle across a Himalayan pass. Learn how to fly an airplane. Read and understand The Art of Computer Programming. Read a QR code with my eyes. Go back to the house I grew up in. Like C++. Write a journal entry every day. Solve a Millennium Prize Problem. Build a computer from scratch. Get over the Auditory Masking effect. Learn how to make a geographical map from scratch. Take a transcontinental train. Fix my television. Spend a day in the International Space Station. Beat a top player in poker. Watch Daft Punk live. Run an ultra marathon. Get a sleeping score of 100 on my smartwatch. Solve integration problems in my head. Find my first best friend. Learn how to play a Double bass. Drink coffee again. 😔 Become an archaeologist.
Since it was I who suggested this prompt at IWCB, I’ve collected all posts that were written on it: ascelpius Divjot Ruben Schade Sid Verma vindo Yash Garg
